newsitem.title: NORWAY: Wall Street gains boost Oslo Bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street gains boost Oslo Bourse index.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange climbed to an all-time high on Monday led by blue chips following gains on Wall Street, dealers said.
The Total index at the Oslo Bourse closed 0.9 percent higher at 1,187.96 points, beating the June 3 life peak of 1,178,74 points. Turnover was healthy at 1.1 billion crowns.
"The market is firm and there seems to be a positive undertone," one broker said.
But another said: "I think the market can get nervous. There is always speculation about the American interest rates."
Industrial group Norsk Hydro, Norway's largest listed company, was the most traded share at 162 million crowns. The share rose 2.13 percent to 383 crowns.
Heavy gains were also made by construction and engineering group Kvaerner, which announced various contracts in United States, southeast Asia and Europe worth nearly two billion crowns altogether.
Kvaerner A-class shares were up 4.07 percent at 422 crowns and the B-class share rose 5.19 percent to 385 crowns.
